document_title: First Amended Tax Capture Waiver Policy
pinpoint: Sec. I (statutory basis MCL 211.7gg; waiver authority MCL 211.1025a(1)); Sec. II (governs over conflicting DLBA policy); Sec. III (application); Sec. IV(C) (Projects and Infill Housing Lots); Sec. IV(D) (de minimis); Sec. VI(A) (calculation)
requirement_supported: Whether and on what terms the DLBA's five-year, fifty-percent tax capture is waived for an Infill Housing Lot or Projects purchase
notes: ANSWERS a material open question, unfavourably. Sec. IV(A)-(B) waive the capture free of charge for Side/Accessory/Oversize/Neighborhood Lots and for Auction/Own-It-Now. Sec. IV(C) expressly covers 'Other Programs (including, but not limited to, Projects and Infill Housing Lots)' and waives ONLY IF the owner compensates the DLBA in full for the estimated remaining capture, or did not receive reasonable advance notice that compensation may be required. Sec. IV(D) permits a free waiver at staff discretion where the estimated capture is under $250. Sec. VI(A): DLBA calculates the amount in its sole discretion and may demand pro formas, development plans and timetables. Denial is appealable to the Board once per property. Carry the buy-out as a real cost line, not a contingency.

document_title: Neighborhood Development Projects Policy (Procedures Governing the Disposition of Properties to Support City of Detroit Economic Development Projects)
pinpoint: Sec. II (Qualified Properties); Sec. III(A) (zoning gate and option agreement); Sec. III(B)(1) (option deposit); Sec. III(C) (FMV, 12-month price expiry); Sec. III(C)(3)(b) (pricing credits); Sec. V(A)-(B) (approval thresholds)
requirement_supported: Projects pathway: qualified uses, zoning gate, option-agreement mechanism, pricing credits, and the quantified threshold at which DLBA Board approval is required
notes: Adopted 11.11.2025, same day as SRC-001, and expressly NOT superseded by it. Sec. II qualifies new construction and affordable housing, so this is a live pathway for Krabby. Sec. V RESOLVES the Board-approval question for this pathway with a quantified threshold: CEO or designee may transfer up to FOUR parcels to the same transferee in any rolling 12 months, or any transaction with aggregate value at or under $75,000; the Board must approve FIVE or more parcels in a rolling 12 months, any transaction over $75,000, or any exception to the Policy. Sec. III(A)(2) permits an option agreement while a purchaser pursues rezoning or a variance -- a materially useful mechanism where zoning does not yet permit the use.
